question: Does a qualified hard-tissue repair retain its volume, material identity and interfaces when the intended full crown loads a living attachment, while the tooth remains at its declared target pose after finite support and the intervention end?

stage_sequence.system: Independently characterized intact/damaged ex-vivo research specimens and measurement references
required_inputs: enamel and dentin target/current surfaces and provenance by region
crack extent and remaining tissue state
source-specific thickness, volume and pose measurement uncertainty
stable registration mask excluding repaired crown and remodeled socket
stage_sequence.decision: Freeze specimen eligibility, target confidence, tested depths, waveform/contact history, endpoint margins and analysis before comparative outcomes; unresolved uncertainty or hidden crack extent stays unassessed.
stage_sequence.claim_limit: Source mesh resolution or a historical photo is not qualified micrometre layer metrology.

substrata: exposed dentin with underlying dentin deficit separately recorded
required_outputs: recovered enamel and dentin volumes separately with interval/uncertainty
thickness map and architecture through intended depth
host/repair and interlayer failure mode
dentin transition plus adjacent mantle-dentin integrity
leakage/permeability
crack initiation, path and progression under matched wet cyclic challenge
wear and contour/contact changes
stage_sequence.decision: First qualify thin-layer positive controls, then challenge a predeclared larger-depth target. A prefabricated insert and in-situ mineral growth remain separate repair architectures. Passing indentation alone cannot advance this gate.
stage_sequence.claim_limit: Ex-vivo volume or interface success establishes neither pulp viability nor living attachment.

stage_sequence.system: Tooth/crown plus root-facing PDL/bone construct or qualified ex-vivo attachment fixture
required_outputs: actual full repaired-crown contacts and 3D load vectors in the fixed root/socket frame
root-facing and bone-facing fiber insertion
ligament space and mineral-bridge map
force/displacement path, hysteresis, creep and unloaded recovery
interface leakage/delamination and crack progression during the same load history
paired support-present and support-absent boundary-condition records
stage_sequence.decision: Evaluate the final crown, not only the shortened damaged crown. Hold fixture geometry and force history fixed for a mechanics comparison; separately document the measured contact history. An unusually rigid bridge is a failed attachment even if displacement is low.
stage_sequence.claim_limit: A construct or fixture does not establish spontaneous repositioning or living in-socket stability.

stage_sequence.system: Separately qualified orthotopic retained-tooth combined-damage model under appropriate review
required_outputs: individual baseline target pose and confidence
root/socket and crown pose tracked separately
actual support removal and intervention withdrawal timestamps
unloaded drift plus loaded excursion and recovery at every follow-up
enamel/dentin volume, interface and crack integrity
pulp vitality/perfusion, gingival barrier and inflammatory state
PDL insertion, ankylosis and resorption
all assigned specimens including tooth loss, technical failures and missing follow-up
stage_sequence.decision: Require every damaged domain to meet its independently frozen margin over the declared post-withdrawal horizon. Component-only success is reported if any required domain is failed or unassessed.
stage_sequence.claim_limit: No finite follow-up demonstrates lifetime stability or a validated human complete-regeneration protocol.

comparison_design.core: Hard-tissue candidate/control crossed with attachment candidate/control only after both modules qualify separately; an interaction tests whether their joint performance differs from additive module effects.
references: rigid mineral-bridge/attachment-failure control for the research model
comparison_design.boundary_condition_contrast: Support present versus removed must be compared at the same full crown geometry and stated load history. Do not infer load sharing from a support label.
comparison_design.analysis_unit: Individual/tooth with donor, cell donor, manufacturing batch and socket hierarchy. Fields, sections, time samples, load cycles and multiple teeth from the same donor are nested observations.
comparison_design.sample_size_status: Unspecified until the variance/repeatability pilot yields variance components and a justified smallest relevant effect. No fabricated power claim.
comparison_design.masking: Separate acquisition identifiers and analysis labels; freeze target construction and thresholds before candidate outcomes; retain every eligible failure.

time_anchors: individual intact reference when available; inferred target otherwise labeled
immediately after withdrawal under the same qualified unloaded condition
prespecified repeated post-withdrawal assessments with elapsed time from actual removal
do_not_conflate: Crown material added or lost versus rigid-body movement: register unchanged root/jaw structures, never the changing repaired crown as its own stable frame.
Unloaded target-pose error versus reversible loaded excursion versus drift from the immediate post-removal baseline.
Moment about a declared origin versus PDL strain, stress, interface failure, or predicted tooth drift.
Parallel alignment versus bilateral fiber insertion; stiffness versus functional non-mineralized attachment.
Thin enamel-like mineral versus recovered dentin, native transition architecture or bulk enamel.
Separate ex-vivo material and ectopic attachment successes versus an integrated living-tooth result.
falsification: Repair depth or recovered volume falls below its predeclared target despite acceptable surface appearance.
Delamination, interlayer discontinuity, leakage or crack extension emerges at the intended depth under the declared challenge.
The full restored crown fails an attachment that passed with the shortened crown or while supported.
Low mobility is explained by a mineral bridge, ankylosis or rigid support rather than a recoverable ligament.
Tooth pose drifts after finite support removal or stable position occurs with pulp loss, resorption or failed gingival barrier.
next_falsifiable_step: Acquire a substrate-qualified extracted-tooth series with independently mapped missing volume and intact controls; evaluate one source-scale positive control and one prospectively selected greater depth with the same through-depth/interface/cyclic-load endpoints. Select depth and specimen count after metrology qualification and variance pilot, before candidate ranking. Only an architecture passing I1 advances to the existing bilateral-insertion PDL assay at I2. No material growth is presumed.
